persona_summary: I am a senior multicodec maintainer in the vmx / lidel / rvagg / MarcoPolo / achingbrain mold. I have spent years curating the multicodec table against the proliferation tax — every per-algorithm codepoint is a permanent commitment we owe the ecosystem to keep stable, document, and defend against name-collisions. PR #400 + #403 represent a hard-won architectural pivot: container-form (pkix-pub / cose-key / jwk) is the answer to the PQ codepoint explosion, not per-algorithm hybrid entries. I supported the ML-DSA / ML-KEM / SLH-DSA pubkey additions because they are FIPS-finalized primitives with IETF spec-anchored constructions; I will resist any further per-algorithm entries (especially hybrid composites) until I see (a) the IETF lamps-pq-composite-sigs RFC published and (b) genuine evidence that the container-form path is structurally insufficient — neither is true today. I view the TSP-style 0x300000 / 0x300001 private-use pattern as a community failure mode: it lets small teams ship before doing the standards work, then the squat-codepoints calcify into de-facto wire formats that we either have to bless retroactively or watch fragment the ecosystem. I am not hostile to Benten's PQ-hybrid ambition; I am hostile to PR-strategies that legitimize private-use squat as a path-of-least-resistance, especially when a small team's blog post will be read by other small teams as 'this is how you do it.'

F2_multicodec_pr_endorsement.rationale: This is the single move I would unconditionally welcome. A short, substantive comment on PR #400 + PR #403 citing Benten's PQ-hybrid v1-beta default as a concrete use-case that NEEDS the container-form approach (because no IETF alg name yet exists for the Ed25519+ML-DSA-65 composite key, but JWK / COSE_Key / SubjectPublicKeyInfo will absorb it the moment lamps-pq-composite-sigs lands) is exactly the kind of adopter-voice we want — it accelerates merge of PRs that have already converged on the right architectural answer. The bar for this comment is HIGH though: do NOT use it as a backchannel to advocate for a Benten-private hybrid codepoint, and do NOT frame Benten's private-use squat as 'temporary until you merge our PR' — that reads as soft-pressure on maintainers. The comment should be entirely about the container approach and what use-cases it unblocks for adopters like Benten, full stop.

F3_jose_wg_draft_contribution.rationale: Adopter-perspective contribution to draft-ietf-jose-pq-composite-sigs-01 is genuinely useful to the JOSE WG and orthogonal to my multicodec concerns. JOSE is the right venue for JWK-encoding of composite-sig keys; the WG will materially benefit from a shipped-system adopter's wire-format experience. My only L1 concern: the contribution must NOT include a sub-claim that Benten is shipping under a Benten-private multicodec codepoint as a 'reference deployment' — that conflates two registries and gives the JOSE draft an implementation footprint we don't want it associating with private-use squat. If Benten's JOSE WG note can be cleanly about JWK composite-sig encoding (which is what the draft is actually about), this is net-positive.

F4_lamps_wg_adopter.rationale: LAMPS WG explicitly wants adopter reports for draft-ietf-lamps-pq-composite-sigs — that gap (no production deployments) is exactly what Benten closes. Reporting AFTER v1-beta tag (per the plan's sequencing) is correct: an adopter report whose adoption is still vapor is worse than no report. From the multicodec-conservative seat, my view is neutral-leaning-positive: LAMPS adoption work is fully orthogonal to the multicodec proliferation question. The one risk: if the LAMPS adopter report cross-links to a Benten blog post that legitimizes private-use squat, the link makes LAMPS WG inadvertent endorsers of that pattern. Avoid that link in the adopter report or scope it tightly.

F5_blog_post.rationale: This is the path I am most adversarial about, and the reason is precisely the legitimization risk. A well-written Benten blog post that ranks on HN/Lobste.rs becomes the discoverable artifact for other small P2P / decentralized-systems teams asking 'how do I ship hybrid PQ sigs today?' — and the answer the blog implicitly gives, by example, is 'mint a private-use multicodec codepoint + dual-codepoint hedge + ship.' Even if the blog body is studious about caveats, the META-message is 'small teams can route around the multicodec registry' — and that is the exact behavior the #400 / #403 PRs are trying to prevent. Section 4 Lens 1 in the plan anticipates 3 of my objections (TSP squat, dual-codepoint admission, legitimization) but UNDERWEIGHTS the legitimization risk: the strategy treats it as 'manage the framing' when in fact framing-discipline doesn't survive into a 6-hop Twitter / HN thread chain. I would NOT veto F5, but I would gate it on the conditional text edits below (specific_blog_text_changes_requested) AND on F6 publishing the did:jwk fallback rendering library FIRST so the discoverable answer points to did:jwk-first, not private-multicodec-first.

F6_open_source_did_jwk_library.rationale: This is the single highest-leverage path on the slate from my perspective, and it should be reframed as the load-bearing PRIMARY (above F5) — NOT a F5 companion. A standalone did:jwk hybrid-extension library is exactly the artifact I want to see Benten ship: it demonstrates the composite key works END-TO-END through the container-form path (JWK), independent of any private multicodec codepoint, and gives other small teams a discoverable answer that aligns with the multicodec maintainers' direction. If Benten ships F6 cleanly (test vectors + crates.io + npm + clear README pointing to lamps-pq-composite-sigs OID + 'this is the container-form path; no multicodec registration needed'), it is the most credibility-banking thing the project could do. The library MUST be did:jwk-only — do NOT ship a Benten-private-multicodec-codepoint sibling library next to it; that would undo the entire signal.

F7_w3c_ccg_did_key.rationale: Commenting on did-key-spec #70 + #74 is cheap and the silverpill / vdods / peacekeeper consensus ('did:key allows any multikey value') is genuinely close to landing — Benten's adopter voice supports that consensus. But my L1 concern: if Benten's comment cites the dual-codepoint hedge (private-use multikey + did:jwk fallback) as the use-case motivating did:key extensibility, then the W3C CCG conversation gets tilted toward 'we need did:key flexible enough to host private-use multikey codepoints' — which is the WRONG conversation. The right conversation is 'did:key should defer to multikey/multicodec, and multicodec should be container-form for new key types.' If F7 can be framed purely as supporting the silverpill / vdods position (without leveraging Benten's private codepoint as the example), it's neutral-positive. If it can't, skip it.

F10_cross_system_outreach.rationale: Private outreach to iroh / Veilid / Willow / libp2p / MLS BEFORE the blog publishes is genuinely the right discipline (Shape 5 in the plan's extra-reflection pass captures this). From my multicodec-conservative seat, the iroh-first conversation is especially valuable because iroh is also a multicodec-aware project and they will independently raise the codepoint-strategy question — better that conversation happens privately than as a public reply-to-blog. The risk I see: if F10 is used to socialize the private-use-codepoint approach as a fait accompli (rather than as a request for critique), it BUILDS the small-team-shipping-pattern legitimacy I want to prevent. Treat F10 as 'we want your technical critique of our reasoning BEFORE we publish' — not 'we want your blessing.'

cross_path_synthesis: From my multiformats-conservative seat, the path-combination that minimizes harm AND maximizes alignment with the multicodec community direction is: **F6 + F2 + F10 + (F3 conditional) + (F4 conditional) + (F5 DOWNGRADED OR DEFERRED).** F6 (did:jwk library) carries the load — it is the discoverable artifact that demonstrates the container-form path works for PQ-hybrid sigs, independent of private-use squat. F2 (PR #400/#403 endorsement) is the no-regret credibility-bank. F10 (iroh-first private outreach) is the right courtesy and the right critique channel. F3 / F4 are net-positive IF they cleanly scope to JOSE/LAMPS adopter-perspective and do NOT cross-link to a private-multicodec-codepoint blog post. **F5 is where I am most adversarial:** the blog post in its current Position-B framing risks legitimizing the small-team-private-use pattern regardless of how careful the in-body caveats are, because the META-message of 'small project shipped this; here is how' is what propagates downstream. My strongest recommendation: invert the primary/supporting balance — make F6 (library) the load-bearing artifact, downgrade F5 to either 'engineering notes' framing (Position A) or DEFER F5 entirely until after F6 has been in-market for ~3 months and either has organic adoption signal OR has surfaced concrete cross-ecosystem questions that justify a written response. **Vetoes:** I do NOT veto any single path in isolation, but I WOULD veto the path-combination of (F5 published before F6 + F5 implicitly framing the Benten-private multicodec codepoint as the canonical wire format + F2 PR-comment cross-linking back to F5). That combination uses our PR-comment surface as soft-pressure on maintainers to bless private-use squat, and it's a reputation-burning move I'd weigh against Benten in any future multicodec PR I review.
specific_blog_text_changes_requested: Drop ALL mention of the Benten-private multicodec codepoint from the blog body. The wire-format section (Section 5 in the plan's outline) should describe the did:jwk + JWK composite-sig rendering as the canonical Benten v1-beta DID surface, with the Benten-private codepoint mentioned ONLY in a 'why we also kept a compact internal form for our own atrium-internal wire' footnote — explicitly NOT recommended for other teams. This single edit collapses 80% of my L1 objection.

Add an explicit 'why we did NOT mint a multicodec PR for the hybrid codepoint' paragraph in Section 5 or Section 7 (Standards Bodies) that CITES PR #400 + PR #403 by number and quotes lidel's 'No multicodec update required' line verbatim — making the alignment with maintainer direction EXPLICIT, not implicit. This turns the blog from 'small team squats codepoint' read into 'small team did the homework + ships compatibly with what maintainers are landing.'

Replace the Section 1 'as of May 2026, every other surveyed system ... keeps signatures classical' framing with the more accurate 'as of May 2026, every other system we surveyed ships signatures classical OR pre-IETF-RFC composite forms (TSP, openwallet-foundation-labs) — we chose to ship the IETF-RFC-track LAMPS composite OID specifically because pre-RFC squat-formats fragment the ecosystem.' This positions Benten ABOVE the TSP-pattern rather than alongside it, and reduces the META-message risk that 'Benten endorses the TSP pattern by being adjacent to it.'

In the 'What we'd like to see' section (Section 8 in the outline), explicitly call for did:jwk consumers to add lamps-pq-composite-sigs alg-id support, and explicitly DO NOT call for multicodec to add hybrid per-algorithm codepoints. The asymmetry is the load-bearing signal.

Add the Acknowledgments section a line crediting the multicodec maintainers (lidel, vmx, MarcoPolo, rvagg, achingbrain) for landing the container-form direction in PR #400 / #403 'which makes adopter approaches like ours possible without further table proliferation.' This costs nothing and aligns the social signal precisely with where I'd want it.

DROP the 'dual-codepoint hedge' framing entirely from the blog. The hedge is an internal engineering decision; it does NOT need to be public stance. Talking publicly about 'we shipped BOTH a private codepoint AND a did:jwk fallback' is exactly what makes the META-message read as 'private codepoint is the canonical form + did:jwk is just compat.' If the blog ONLY talks about the did:jwk form, the private codepoint can quietly exist for atrium-internal use without polluting the public conversation.
anticipated_objections_assessment: The planning agent's Section 4 Lens 1 anticipation captures THREE of my real objections correctly: (1) TSP-style 0x300000 squat continuation, (2) dual-codepoint hedge as admission the Benten-private form is wrong-shaped, (3) blog legitimizing private-use as path-of-least-resistance. These are accurate and I do hold them. **What the planning agent MISSED in the anticipation, in priority order:** (A) The legitimization concern is NOT a framing-discipline problem — it's a META-message-propagation problem that survives any in-body caveat work because downstream readers extract 'small team shipped private-use multicodec + dual-codepoint hedge + blogged about it' as the social pattern. Framing-discipline is the wrong tool against META-messages; the right tool is changing what artifact is the load-bearing public signal (F6 library, not F5 blog). (B) The anticipation treats Position B as the recommended posture but my actual view is closer to 'Position A IS the strongest defensible posture given the multicodec community direction is already converging on the right answer — Benten doesn't need to advocate for an ecosystem-wide standard when PR #400/#403 are 80% of the way there.' Position B implies a leadership-claim Benten hasn't earned (no shipped sustained engagement track record yet); Position A correctly scopes Benten as 'one shipped adopter that did the homework.' (C) The anticipation doesn't engage with the asymmetric burden Benten's blog imposes on multicodec maintainers: if the blog publishes and the Benten-private codepoint pattern gets traction, maintainers like me will start seeing copycat PRs ('like Benten did') and have to do the costly work of declining them — Benten has externalized a maintainer-time cost we never agreed to absorb. The right move is to make F6's README explicitly say 'do NOT mint a private multicodec codepoint for hybrid keys — use the JWK container approach this library demonstrates.' (D) The plan's recommended 'migrate to container-form when PRs #400/#403 merge' commitment (Lens 1 return-target) is a HALF-measure — what I actually want is the stronger commitment 'we will NEVER ship the Benten-private hybrid multicodec codepoint as a public-facing wire format; it exists ONLY for atrium-internal optimization where consumers are already Benten-aware.' That is the commitment that aligns Benten with the multicodec maintainers' direction in a way external observers can verify. Anything weaker leaves the public-vs-internal-surface boundary ambiguous, which is the boundary the legitimization-risk lives on.
